I will keep my land in the standard Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I am 68, so I do not want a complicated mix of crops that needs too much hand labor or market timing. I know this rotation well, it fits the local climate and irrigation conditions, and it spreads my workload across the year. Because I am well educated, I will use improved or hybrid seed, soil-testing logic, and relatively disciplined fertilizer and water management instead of farming by habit alone. For wheat, I will focus on stable tillering, one strong base fertilizer application, careful spring nitrogen topdressing, and a few irrigations at key stages. For maize, I will use a dense but manageable planting pattern, place fertilizer more precisely, irrigate when tasseling and grain filling need it, and keep pesticide use limited to real pest or disease pressure. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient, common locally, and easier for me to manage with machinery than repeated deep ploughing.
